newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close up, off highs, as Dow falters.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close up, off highs, as Dow falters.

text.p: French stocks finished higher on Friday, propelled by a rise in bond prices on expectations of European interest rate cuts.
But the bourse retreated from its best levels after Wall Street's weak performance in early trade.
"The prospect of European interest rate cuts right now is much more important for the bourse than the wavering on Wall Street, which is holding up rather well considering the levels," a trader said.
The Dow was hovering around 6,000 points when the Paris market closed.
The French blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 10.81 points or 0.5 percent at 2,162.43, while the CAC-40 October futures contract rose 6.5 points to 2,163.50. Volume was a brisk 4.7 billion francs.
Even if the Bundesbank does not cut its rates, analysts say the Bank of France has scope to trim rates to bring them closer in line to German rates.

Shares in chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc closed up 3.16 percent at 147 francs after announcing a bigger than expected 13 percent rise in third quarter profit. It said the increase would have been 25 percent if it weren't for a product recall. Some analysts were considering raising their earnings forecasts.
